verification_status: FULL TEXT VERIFIED (CC-BY, Europe PMC PMC13498696); journal Scopus-indexed per SJR, article record not directly verified
method: Mixture (LC-IRT) model: classes with class-specific normal theta distributions; two-step (fixed-parameter) estimator: step 1 measurement model incl. DIF direct effects, step 2 covariate->class with measurement fixed; compared to FIML by simulation
data: Simulations (DIF and multidimensional conditions); empirical: n=300 Italian psychology undergraduates, statistics test (Dublin-descriptor dimensions)
contribution: Brings Bakk-Kuha two-step logic to LC-IRT with DIF and multidimensionality; guards against interpretational confounding
results: Low bias when entropy is high (>.80 in sims); FIML more sensitive to misspecification; two-step more biased under low separation. Empirical: BIC chose 2 classes, AIC 3; the 2-class solution 'mainly distinguished students with higher versus lower statistical competence'
limitations: No response times; class enumeration done before covariates (performance of that strategy under two-step left for future work); no one-class/null generating condition reported in what we read; small empirical n
relevance: Gives the estimation template (measurement first, covariates/DIF second) for our LC-IRT with country/gender covariates; its empirical 2-class solution is itself an example of classes that may be ability slices
remaining_gap: Does not test whether classes exceed a continuous theta (no null calibration), no timing data
